_doc: THE ONE UNTRUSTED SLOT. This table is the entire attack surface of the `html` bounded-value primitive (docs/design/html-value-sanitizer.md). JSON stays canon; HTML is a bounded VALUE inside it, never the container — so instead of proving a negative over a whole document, the gate is a whitelist over one node type at a known schema location. Vocabulary MEASURED from 55 content-unique corpus documents: outside <script>, real Claude-written HTML uses only ~60 element types and ~6 meaningful attributes. Anything absent here is REJECTED LOUDLY, never stripped — a silently-stripping sanitizer is a silent-drop bug wearing a security label.
_rejected_note: Deliberately absent: script, style, iframe, object, embed, form, input, button, link, meta, base, audio, video, img, canvas, template, slot, portal, math, foreignObject, and every unknown/custom element. `button` is excluded despite 184 corpus uses because a button with no script is a lie to the reader — interactivity belongs to primitives where the ENGINE writes the script. `img` is excluded because a raster source is either a remote fetch or a data URI, and inline SVG covers the corpus's real usage.
_attribute_rejected_note: ALWAYS rejected, on every element: every on* handler, style, src, srcset, formaction, xlink:href, data-*, contenteditable, tabindex, autofocus, and anything not listed above. `style=` is rejected despite 684 corpus occurrences for two reasons: it carries url(), a network vector that would require a CSS parser inside the gate; and inline colour hard-codes a value outside the palette, breaking `--style` and quietly violating Covenant II. The MITIGATION IS ALREADY SHIPPED — the utility layer (utility_css.json) gives authors themeable classes bound to palette tokens, so `class="u-amber u-tight"` replaces `style="color:#f59e0b"` and themes correctly under every style. Rejecting style= is reasonable rather than punitive precisely because that layer exists.
